newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen continuing record run.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen continuing record run.

text.p: Belgian shares put on a mixed show on Thursday, but a strong performance by market laggard Bekaert helped maintain the Bel-20 Index on its record breaking run.

Dealers said they saw no grounds for the rally to stop, with the market supported by fresh position taking on the first day of a new account and in anticipation the Bundesbank, meeting later, would keep its interest-rate tiller steady.
By 1015 GMT the Bel-20 Index .BFX was up 10.62 points, or 0.52 percent, at 2,058.29 points, surpassing its previous all-time high of 2,056.75 set on Wednesday.
Thirteen issues were higher, with Bekaert up 975 francs, or 5.26 percent, at 19,500 francs.
The gain helped Bekaert partially reverse its weak performance since the start of the year, when it has underperformed the index by around 15 percent.
Analyst Patrick Millecam at brokerage Corluy expected the market to focus soon on other stocks which have lagged recently, citing CNP/NPM as one example.
Shares in CNP/NPM unit Groupe Bruxelles Lambert have risen nearly 10 percent since the start of the year, while its own shares have added just 2.5 percent, he noted.
